world.name: JavaScript
world.title: The JavaScript Workshop
world.subtitle: Build reliable programs from first values to asynchronous work queues

paths.name: Foundations
paths.description: Start here if you are new to JavaScript. Build small programs that turn raw input into useful records and report failures clearly.
paths.topics: Bindings, comparisons, arrays, records, functions, control flow, JSON and errors

paths.name: Application
paths.description: Use familiar language basics to solve the problems that arise when programs share state, pass methods as callbacks and coordinate asynchronous work.
paths.topics: Closures, identity, array transforms, promises, stale results, method receivers and bounded work queues

paths.name: Full Workshop
paths.description: Work through both zones in order, starting with values and ending by implementing and testing an asynchronous job queue.
paths.topics: The complete path from JavaScript basics to a concurrency capstone

quests.objective: Use const and let deliberately and distinguish changing a binding from mutating a value.
quests.boss_brief: Implement makeBadge(rawName). The input is a string. Remove surrounding whitespace, uppercase the result, and return a fresh record with fields name and visits, with visits starting at 0. makeBadge('  Jo ') should return { name: 'JO', visits: 0 }. Two calls should return separate records.
quests.side_quest: Call makeBadge twice with the same name. Increment the visits property on the first result and check that the second stays at zero.
quests.hint1: String methods return a string. Keep the result of each step.
quests.hint2: Chain rawName.trim().toUpperCase() and use an object literal in the return expression.
quests.debrief: Use a const binding for the cleaned name and create { name, visits: 0 } inside the function. A new object literal on each call prevents two callers from accidentally sharing visit counts.

quests.objective: Predict strict equality, boolean conditions and nullish defaults.
quests.boss_brief: Implement readLimit(raw, fallback). raw is a string, null or undefined. Return fallback for a nullish or blank input. For any other string, use Number to convert it and return the value if it is a nonnegative integer. Return null for an invalid value. Check '0', ' 12 ', '  ', '3.5' and 'oops'.
quests.side_quest: Try the string '0x10'. If only decimal digits are allowed, add a digit-only check before Number and describe the changed contract.
quests.hint1: Test raw === null || raw === undefined before calling trim.
quests.hint2: An empty trimmed string needs the fallback. Then convert with Number and test Number.isInteger(value) && value >= 0.
quests.debrief: Treat missing and blank inputs together. Convert nonblank input once, validate it, and return either that number or null. The caller can distinguish an invalid string from a missing preference.

quests.objective: Represent ordered collections with arrays and named attributes with objects.
quests.boss_brief: Implement quantitiesFor(shipments, id). Return a new array containing the quantity of each record with a matching id, in the original order. Keep zero quantities. Return an empty array when there are no matches and leave the input untouched.
quests.side_quest: Add a separate lookup that returns the first matching record or null. Explain why it should stop at the first match.
quests.hint1: Compare the shipment's id with the requested id. Compare IDs, not quantities.
quests.hint2: A for...of loop over shipments can push shipment.quantity into the result after a strict equality check.
quests.debrief: Collect into a fresh array and append a quantity whenever shipment.id === id. A zero quantity is still a result. The original array and its records are unchanged.

quests.objective: Write functions with explicit inputs, outputs and valid ranges.
quests.boss_brief: Implement shippingCents(subtotalCents, delivery = 'standard'). Inputs are a nonnegative integer and either 'standard' or 'express'. Express always costs 1200 cents. Standard costs 500 cents when the subtotal is below 5000 and zero at or above 5000. Return the number of cents.
quests.side_quest: Write a second function that formats the result for display while leaving shippingCents focused on calculation.
quests.hint1: Check the delivery mode before evaluating the standard shipping threshold.
quests.hint2: Return 1200 immediately for express, otherwise use subtotalCents >= 5000 to choose between 0 and 500.
quests.debrief: Test standard at 4999 and 5000, express at 5000, and a call with the second argument omitted. These checks distinguish the delivery rule from the default and its boundary.

quests.objective: Trace decisions and iterate without silently dropping valid data.
quests.boss_brief: Implement pendingSummary(tasks). Each task has a boolean done and a nonnegative integer minutes. Return { count, minutes } for unfinished tasks only. Count unfinished tasks that take zero minutes. Return { count: 0, minutes: 0 } for an empty array.
quests.side_quest: Return a second count for unfinished tasks over 30 minutes and test tasks at exactly 30 and 31.
quests.hint1: Check done independently from minutes. Zero minutes does not mean complete.
quests.hint2: Skip completed tasks. For each remaining task, increment count and add task.minutes.
quests.debrief: Initialize both totals to zero, visit each task and skip only tasks marked done. A zero-minute unfinished task increments count without changing minutes.

quests.objective: Separate valid JSON syntax from the shape a program expects.
quests.boss_brief: Implement decodeItem(text) for valid JSON text. Accept a non-array record with its own string id and nonnegative integer count. The id must be nonempty after trimming. Return a fresh { id, count } with the trimmed id. For valid JSON of any other shape, return null. Malformed JSON may throw in this lesson.
quests.side_quest: Wrap only the JSON.parse call in a try/catch and return different error labels for malformed JSON and an invalid item shape.
quests.hint1: Check the top-level type and shape, then require id and count with Object.hasOwn.
quests.hint2: Trim only a string id, and test Number.isInteger(value.count) && value.count >= 0. Build a fresh record.
quests.debrief: Test a valid count of zero and invalid inputs including null, an array, an empty ID and a numeric string count. Those distinguish shape checking from truthiness and automatic conversion.

quests.objective: Distinguish expected validation failures from exceptions and test both paths.
quests.boss_brief: Implement parseCount(text) for string input. Return { ok: false, reason: 'syntax' } for malformed JSON. For valid JSON that is not a nonnegative integer number, return { ok: false, reason: 'count' }. Return { ok: true, value } otherwise. Test '0', '-1', '1.5', '"2"' and '{'.
quests.side_quest: Write a tiny assertion helper, run the five sample checks and show the failing case's input if any check fails.
quests.hint1: Put the JSON.parse assignment inside the try block. Keep the integer check afterward.
quests.hint2: Translate SyntaxError to the syntax result and rethrow other errors. A nonnegative integer satisfies Number.isInteger(value) && value >= 0.
quests.debrief: Parsing and validation describe different failures. Returning a distinct reason for each lets a caller handle both while preserving unexpected exceptions.

quests.objective: Use lexical scope to expose a small interface and test whether instances share state.
quests.boss_brief: Implement makeTicketDispenser(prefix). Return an object with next() and issued(). next returns strings such as 'LAB-1', 'LAB-2' and increases the count. issued returns how many tickets the instance has given out. New instances must start independently.
quests.side_quest: Return the next function by itself and invoke it as a callback. Explain how it still reaches its own count.
quests.hint1: Place count inside the factory so no other factory call shares it.
quests.hint2: Increment before formatting the prefix, a hyphen and the new count.
quests.debrief: Call next twice on one dispenser and once on another with a different prefix. Check each issued result and ensure calling issued never changes the count.

quests.objective: Update nested data without surprising callers who hold older references.
quests.boss_brief: Implement setTheme(profile, theme) for plain data records with own enumerable fields. Return new profile and settings records with settings.theme changed. Preserve the other fields, leave the original unchanged and keep the tags array shared.
quests.side_quest: Write addTag(profile, tag) that creates a new tags array only when tag is absent. Decide what identity the function should return when nothing changes.
quests.hint1: Check that both the outer profile and its settings have new identities.
quests.hint2: Use a nested spread and put theme after the existing settings properties so it replaces the prior theme.
quests.debrief: Compare the original and result at each layer. The result and its settings should differ in identity, while result.tags === profile.tags should be true.

quests.objective: Build a data pipeline with explicit selection, transformation and sorting rules.
quests.boss_brief: Implement leaderboard(players). Select records with active === true, sort by numeric score descending and return a new array of their names. For equal scores, preserve their input order. Leave the input order and records untouched.
quests.side_quest: Aggregate player scores into a Map keyed by team ID and describe how you would break ties explicitly.
quests.hint1: Run filter first. It gives you a fresh outer array to sort.
quests.hint2: Use (a, b) => b.score - a.score, then map each remaining record to name.
quests.debrief: Test a score of 10 beside 2, two equal scores, and an inactive leader. Also verify that the order of the input records did not change.

quests.objective: Follow settlement order and preserve input order when coordinating independent work.
quests.boss_brief: Implement loadInOrder(ids, load). For each ID, call the supplied async load(id) once and return a promise for the values in input order. Start the calls without awaiting one before starting the next. If a load rejects, let the returned promise reject.
quests.side_quest: Write a separate variant using Promise.allSettled that reports failures beside their input IDs.
quests.hint1: An array of IDs can map to an array of promises.
quests.hint2: Use Promise.all on ids.map(id => load(id)). Promise.all preserves the input positions.
quests.debrief: Check that load is invoked for every ID before any of the pending promises resolves. Complete them in reverse order and verify the returned array still follows ids.

quests.objective: Prevent older asynchronous results from replacing newer state.
quests.boss_brief: Implement makeLatest(load, publish). It returns an async function run(query). Call load(query) for each run. If the run is still most recent when it handles the outcome, publish { ok: true, value } for fulfillment or { ok: false, error } for rejection or a synchronous throw. Ignore older outcomes. The run promise fulfills after handling either outcome. Assume publish does not throw.
quests.side_quest: Pass an AbortSignal to a cancellation-aware loader and abort the preceding signal when a new run starts. Keep the token check and test a loader that ignores the signal.
quests.hint1: Create and store a unique Symbol token synchronously when run starts, before the first await.
quests.hint2: Call and await load(query) inside try/catch. Form an outcome in either case and publish it only if the token is still current.
quests.debrief: Try a slow success followed by a fast success, then a slow rejection followed by a fast success. The first call should not publish anything in either test.

quests.objective: Preserve the intended this when a method crosses a callback boundary.
quests.boss_brief: Implement makeRecorder(ledger). ledger has an add(amount) method that depends on this and returns its updated total. Return a standalone callback that forwards amount to ledger.add and returns the method's result. Creating the callback must not change the total.
quests.side_quest: Create recorders for two separate ledgers and alternate calls. Explain how the callbacks keep their targets separate.
quests.hint1: Read the difference between returning a function and calling it now.
quests.hint2: Either bind ledger.add to ledger or return amount => ledger.add(amount).
quests.debrief: Pass the result to a helper that calls operation(amount). The total on the original ledger should change exactly once and the callback should return the new total.

quests.objective: Run independent asynchronous jobs with a concurrency limit and stable result positions.
quests.boss_brief: Implement runQueue(tasks, limit). Each task is a zero-argument function that returns a promise or throws synchronously. Reject with RangeError for a limit that is not a positive integer. Run at most limit tasks at once and return one result per input in input order. Use { ok: true, value } or { ok: false, error }, and continue processing after a failure. The empty queue returns [].
quests.side_quest: Add a signal that stops claiming new work when aborted and define what outcome unstarted tasks receive. Decide separately how already-running tasks can cooperate with cancellation.
quests.hint1: Use a shared cursor and give each worker an async loop. Claim an index before calling the task.
quests.hint2: Catch both sync throws and promise rejections by calling and awaiting the task in one try block. Store the outcome at its original index.
quests.debrief: Use test tasks that signal when they start and resolve only when you release them. Check that no more than limit run at a time, that a failed task does not stop later ones and that reversing completion order does not change result positions.
